statement: Under Assumption 1.1, the following consequences hold. (i) From every sequence of Poisson meshes tending to zero one can extract, after coupling, a further subsequence along which the graphs almost surely form a deterministic good sequence in the sense of [10, Lemma 2.5]. Along such a sequence, critical crossings of Jordan quadrilaterals converge, also for graph domains whose boundaries and marked points converge in curve order. Finite joint crossing tests and tests with finitely many separated prescribed squares have the common triangular-percolation limit. (ii) Chordal color explorations in converging Jordan graph domains converge to chordal SLE6. At a pre-query stop on a crosscut, the remaining target face, its boundary banks, and its conformal maps converge in the sense of the stopped-domain results of [10]. A bank is an individual boundary arc in prime-end order; distinct banks may have touching physical images. Each relevant bank is individually simple. (iii) For some c0 > 0, in the mesh-first limit the probability of four bulk arms with any specified color order is at most C(r/s)1+c0 , and that of six bulk arms with any specified color order is at most C(r/s)2+c0 . Three free arms at a regular boundary, measured in a conformal chart, have an upper bound with exponent strictly larger than one.
